title: Rigveda 4.30: To Indra
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 4.30: To Indra: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 4.30 is a hymn of 24 verses addressed to Indra. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 4, the family book of Vāmadeva. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 288r-290r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 4.30.1-2 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 6, varga 19); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 288r
translation.original_text:
1naki̍r indra̱ tvad utta̍ro̱ na jyāyā̍m̐ asti vṛtrahan | naki̍r e̱vā yathā̱ tvam ||
2sa̱trā te̱ anu̍ kṛ̱ṣṭayo̱ viśvā̍ ca̱kreva̍ vāvṛtuḥ | sa̱trā ma̱hām̐ a̍si śru̱taḥ ||
translation.text:
1O INDRA, Vr̥itra-slayer, none is better, mightier than thou: Verily there is none like thee.
2Like chariot-wheels these people all together follow after thee: Thou ever art renowned as Great.

translation.original_ref: RV 4.30.3-8 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 6, varga 19); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 288v
translation.original_text:
3viśve̍ ca̱ned a̱nā tvā̍ de̱vāsa̍ indra yuyudhuḥ | yad ahā̱ nakta̱m āti̍raḥ ||
4yatro̱ta bā̍dhi̱tebhya̍ś ca̱kraṁ kutsā̍ya̱ yudhya̍te | mu̱ṣā̱ya i̍ndra̱ sūrya̍m ||
5yatra̍ de̱vām̐ ṛ̍ghāya̱to viśvā̱m̐ ayu̍dhya̱ eka̱ it | tvam i̍ndra va̱nūm̐r aha̍n ||
6yatro̱ta martyā̍ya̱ kam ari̍ṇā indra̱ sūrya̍m | prāva̱ḥ śacī̍bhi̱r eta̍śam ||
7kim ād u̱tāsi̍ vṛtraha̱n magha̍van manyu̱matta̍maḥ | atrāha̱ dānu̱m āti̍raḥ ||
8e̱tad ghed u̱ta vī̱rya1̱̍m indra̍ ca̱kartha̱ pauṁsya̍m | striya̱ṁ yad du̍rhaṇā̱yuva̱ṁ vadhī̍r duhi̱tara̍ṁ di̱vaḥ ||
translation.text:
3Not even all the gathered Gods conquered thee, Indra, in the war, When thou didst lengthen days by night.
4When for the sake of those oppressed, and Kutsa as he battled, Thou stolest away the Sun's car-wheel.
5When, fighting singly, Indra. thou o'ercamest all the furious Gods, thou slewest those who strove with thee.
6When also for a mortal man, Indra, thou speddest forth the Sun, And holpest Etaṣa with might.
7What? Vr̥itra-slayer, art not thou, Maghavan, fiercest in thy wrath? So hast thou quelled the demon too.
8And this heroic deed of might thou, Indra, also hast achieved, That thou didst smite to death the Dame, Heaven's Daughter, meditating ill.

translation.original_ref: RV 4.30.9-16 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 6, varga 20); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 289r
translation.original_text:
9di̱vaś ci̍d ghā duhi̱tara̍m ma̱hān ma̍hī̱yamā̍nām | u̱ṣāsa̍m indra̱ sam pi̍ṇak ||
10apo̱ṣā ana̍saḥ sara̱t sampi̍ṣṭā̱d aha̍ bi̱bhyuṣī̍ | ni yat sī̍ṁ śi̱śnatha̱d vṛṣā̍ ||
11e̱tad a̍syā̱ ana̍ḥ śaye̱ susa̍mpiṣṭa̱ṁ vipā̱śy ā | sa̱sāra̍ sīm parā̱vata̍ḥ ||
12u̱ta sindhu̍ṁ vibā̱lya̍ṁ vitasthā̱nām adhi̱ kṣami̍ | pari̍ ṣṭhā indra mā̱yayā̍ ||
13u̱ta śuṣṇa̍sya dhṛṣṇu̱yā pra mṛ̍kṣo a̱bhi veda̍nam | puro̱ yad a̍sya sampi̱ṇak ||
14u̱ta dā̱saṁ kau̍lita̱ram bṛ̍ha̱taḥ parva̍tā̱d adhi̍ | avā̍hann indra̱ śamba̍ram ||
15u̱ta dā̱sasya̍ va̱rcina̍ḥ sa̱hasrā̍ṇi śa̱tāva̍dhīḥ | adhi̱ pañca̍ pra̱dhīm̐r i̍va ||
16u̱ta tyam pu̱tram a̱gruva̱ḥ parā̍vṛktaṁ śa̱takra̍tuḥ | u̱ktheṣv indra̱ ābha̍jat ||
translation.text:
9Thou, Indra, Mighty One, didst crush Ushas, though Daughter of the Sky. When lifting up herself in pride.
10Then from her chariot Ushas fled, affrighted, from her ruined car. When the strong God had shattered it.
11So there this car of Ushas lay, broken to pieces, in Vipâṣ, And she herself fled far away.
12Thou, Indra, didst with magic power resist the overflowing stream Who spread her waters o'er the land.
13Valiantly didst thou seize and take the store which Ṣushṇa had amassed, When thou didst crush his fortresses.
14Thou, Indra, also smotest down Kulitara's son Ṣambara, The Dâsa, from the lofty hill.
15Of Dâsa Varcin's thou didst slay the hundred thousand and the five, Crushed like the fellies, of a car.
16So Indra, Lord of Heroes, Powers, caused the unwedded damsel's son, The castaway, to share the lauds.

translation.original_ref: RV 4.30.17-23 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 6, varga 22); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 289v
translation.original_text:
17u̱ta tyā tu̱rvaśā̱yadū̍ asnā̱tārā̱ śacī̱pati̍ḥ | indro̍ vi̱dvām̐ a̍pārayat ||
18u̱ta tyā sa̱dya āryā̍ sa̱rayo̍r indra pā̱rata̍ḥ | arṇā̍ci̱trara̍thāvadhīḥ ||
19anu̱ dvā ja̍hi̱tā na̍yo̱ 'ndhaṁ śro̱ṇaṁ ca̍ vṛtrahan | na tat te̍ su̱mnam aṣṭa̍ve ||
20śa̱tam a̍śma̱nmayī̍nām pu̱rām indro̱ vy ā̍syat | divo̍dāsāya dā̱śuṣe̍ ||
21asvā̍payad da̱bhīta̍ye sa̱hasrā̍ tri̱ṁśata̱ṁ hathai̍ḥ | dā̱sānā̱m indro̍ mā̱yayā̍ ||
22sa ghed u̱tāsi̍ vṛtrahan samā̱na i̍ndra̱ gopa̍tiḥ | yas tā viśvā̍ni cicyu̱ṣe ||
23u̱ta nū̱naṁ yad i̍ndri̱yaṁ ka̍ri̱ṣyā i̍ndra̱ pauṁsya̍m | a̱dyā naki̱ṣ ṭad ā mi̍nat ||
translation.text:
17So sapient Indra, Lord of Might, brought Turvaga and Yadu, those Who feared the flood, in safety o'er.
18Arṇa and Chitraratha, both Aryas, thou, Indra, slewest swift, On yonder side of Sarayu,
19Thou, Vr̥itra-slayer, didst conduct those two forlorn, the blind, the lame. None may attain this bliss of thine.
20For Divodâsa, him who brought oblations, Indra overthrew A hundred fortresses of stone.
21The thirty thousand Disas he with magic power and weapons sent To slumber, for Dabhîti's sake.
22As such, O Vr̥itra-slayer, thou art general Lord of kine for all, Thou Shaker of all things that be.
23Indra, whatever deed of might thou hast this day to execute, None be there now to hinder it.

translation.original_ref: RV 4.30.24 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 6, varga 23); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 290r
translation.original_text: <sup>24</sup>vā̱maṁ-vā̍maṁ ta ādure de̱vo da̍dātv arya̱mā | vā̱mam pū̱ṣā vā̱mam bhago̍ vā̱maṁ de̱vaḥ karū̍ḻatī ||
translation.text: <sup>24</sup>O Watchful One, may Aryaman the God give thee all goodly things. May Pûshan, Bhaga, and the God Karûlatî give all things fair.
